correctness.rationale: For \(K_{n_1,\ldots,n_r}\), let \(N\) be the order, \(m\) the smallest part, and \(M\) the largest. Then \(\Delta=N-m\) and \(\alpha=M\). The sum of the \(\Delta+1\) smallest degrees is at least \(2e-(m-1)\Delta>e\), because the edges incident with a smallest part already give \(e\ge m\Delta\); hence \(a\le\Delta\). Gupta's equality criterion then yields \((\Delta-1)M\le\Delta\), forcing complete graphs for \(\Delta\ge3\) and the stated low-degree cases. Direct invariant calculations confirm all four survivors. A fresh independent complete-multipartite enumeration reproduced exactly these four equality types through order 19.
correctness.risk: The correctness proof depends on the published TxGraffiti equality criterion, which was independently checked against Gupta's source text.

originality.rationale: A stronger pre-existing source was missed by the frozen audit. Kadrawi and Levit, submitted 1 July 2026, prove a general equality characterization for the same TxGraffiti inequality. Their Corollary 9 states that for connected graphs with \(\Delta=2\), equality holds exactly when \(R=\alpha\), and for \(\Delta\ge3\) it can hold only when \(\Delta=3\) together with explicit Caro--Wei/residue/slack equalities. Specializing this theorem to complete multipartite graphs reduces the submitted classification to a tiny finite check: \(\Delta=2\) gives only \(P_3,K_3,C_4\); \(\Delta=3\) permits only five part-size patterns, of which the general equality conditions leave only \(K_4\). Thus the final classification is a direct corollary of a stronger theorem publicly available more than three months before this record.
